name: Data Center West, Inc.

profile.address: 800, Willamette Street, College Hill, Eugene, Lane County, Oregon, 97401
profile.reading:
Date Center West - Eugene, the "Date" in the name is very likely a data-entry typo for "Data" carried over from OpenStreetMap, is one of two facilities operated by Data Center West, Inc., an independent, privately held colocation and managed-services provider founded in 2004 and based in Southern Oregon. The company's core market is Medford, Ashland, Klamath Falls, and Grants Pass, and it markets itself as the largest independent colocation and cloud-services provider in Southern Oregon and Northern California. The Eugene site, roughly 165 miles north in the Willamette Valley, is its smaller secondary location, extending that regional footprint north along Interstate 5.

Data Center West publishes real, if modest, technical specifications for its facilities rather than treating them as unpublished. The Eugene site has 500 square feet of raised technical floor space rated to carry more than 800 pounds per square foot, a floor load specification aimed at server racks and storage arrays rather than a general office build-out, with dedicated 110, 208, and 220-volt electrical circuits. Power resilience comes from telco-standard DC power service backed by the building's own diesel generator, and cooling is handled by 5-ton air-conditioning units. Fire detection uses smoke, heat, and thermal alarms rather than a gas-based suppression system, and the site has two separate fiber entry points, a basic but meaningful form of physical carrier diversity for a facility this size. By comparison, the company's larger Medford facility runs to 2,000 square feet with a dedicated Caterpillar 3412 diesel generator and four 5-ton AC units, underscoring that Eugene is deliberately the smaller of the company's two data halls.

What Data Center West does not publish for Eugene is a specific street address on its own site, a megawatt or kilowatt IT-capacity figure, or a formal Tier or uptime certification. That is consistent with the scale of the business. This is a small, regional, privately held colocation operator serving local businesses in a secondary market, not a wholesale or hyperscale operator competing nationally on published capacity numbers. The facility exists to give Eugene-area businesses, likely including local government, healthcare, education, and small-business tenants, reliable rack space and internet connectivity without having to reach north to Portland or contract with a national colocation brand for a modest hosting need.

profile.address: 739, Welch Drive, Medford, Jackson County, Oregon, 97501
profile.reading:
Data Center West, Inc. is an independent, privately held colocation and cloud-services provider that has operated in Oregon's Rogue Valley since 2004. Rather than build for a national hyperscale market, the company positions itself as the largest independent colocation and computing provider in Southern Oregon and Northern California, serving customers in Medford, Ashland, Klamath Falls and Grants Pass, and maintaining the Ashland Fiber Network as part of its regional connectivity.

This facility sits at 739 Welch Drive in Medford, Jackson County, and is the company's primary technical site. Per Data Center West's own published specifications, the Medford building offers roughly 2,000 square feet of climate-controlled, Level 1-connected technical space rated to a 500-pound-per-square-foot floor load, with racks that are seismically braced against earthquake movement, a meaningful design choice in an active seismic region. Backup power is supplied by a 600-amp diesel generator, a Caterpillar 3412 unit, and cooling runs through four to seven tons of redundant HVAC capacity. The company advertises diverse-route, redundant fiber connections and round-the-clock network monitoring, and offers customers a mix of rack, cabinet and cage space on a telco-neutral basis, meaning tenants can bring their own carrier of choice rather than being tied to one upstream provider.

Data Center West also operates a second, smaller facility roughly 175 miles north in Eugene, about 500 square feet, with a direct fiber connection into the city's Central Office 53, along with additional sites in Ashland, Oregon and Redding, California. Some third-party data-center directories list the Medford building under an Eugene-market heading, which can make the two sites easy to conflate; the facility described here, however, is the Medford location on Welch Drive, not the smaller Eugene site.

No independent power-capacity figure in megawatts has been published for the Medford facility, and the company does not disclose a power-usage-effectiveness rating, tenant list, or a breakdown of raised-floor versus support square footage, the kind of detail typically reserved for hyperscale or wholesale colocation providers rather than a regional, privately held operator serving a mid-size metro market. What is public is consistent with a modest, purpose-built regional colocation facility rather than a large multi-tenant data-center campus, and the company's emphasis on seismic bracing, generator backup and redundant fiber reflects the priorities of a business-continuity-focused provider serving small and mid-size enterprise customers across Southern Oregon.

[2026-09-04 follow-up] This row's OSM-derived name reads 'Date Center West - Eugene' but its stored coordinates/address resolve to 739 Welch Drive, Medford OR -- Data Center West's primary Medford facility, not the company's actual Eugene site. Per the operator's own facilities page (datacenterwest.com/our-facilities.html), Data Center West operates a SEPARATE, smaller ~500 sqft Eugene facility with direct fiber to Eugene Central Office 53, plus sites in Ashland OR and Redding CA. Third-party directories (lead only, not cited) list a distinct Eugene address (800 Willamette St) different from this row's Medford coordinates. Conclusion: this appears to be an OSM mistagging/duplicate -- an Eugene-derived name attached to Medford coordinates -- rather than confirmation of a genuine second Medford-area Data Center West location marketed under an Eugene label. The public reading above describes the Medford facility the row's actual address represents and clarifies the naming discrepancy for readers without asserting this row IS the company's Eugene site.

reading:
Data Center West, Inc. is a small, privately held colocation and internet service business in Oregon's Rogue Valley. It describes itself as one of the largest independent providers of colocation and wireless internet service in Southern Oregon, and it operates data centre rooms as part of a regional ISP rather than as a national platform. Its own site names four locations, Medford, Ashland and Eugene in Oregon and Redding in California, and it does not state a founding year, an ownership structure or a headquarters street address. The registry holds two Oregon rows for it.

Unusually for an operator of this size, the company publishes real specifications rather than treating them as confidential, and they are small enough to be worth quoting exactly. The Medford site has 2,000 square feet of technical space rated above 500 pounds per square foot, a 600 amp power service with dedicated 110, 208 and 220 volt circuits, a Caterpillar 3412 diesel standby generator, four five ton air conditioning units, smoke and heat detection alarms, two fibre entry points with two three inch conduits, overhead ladder rack for cable management, and a ten foot by nine foot roll door. The Eugene site has 500 square feet of technical space rated above 800 pounds per square foot, telco DC power service backed by the building's own diesel generator, five ton air conditioning, smoke and heat and thermal alarms, and two fibre entry points with six three inch conduits.

Note carefully what those numbers are. A 600 amp service is utility power at the panel, the electrical service the room can draw. A Caterpillar 3412 is standby diesel generation, sized to ride through an outage. Neither is an IT load, and Data Center West publishes no IT load, no power usage effectiveness figure and no uptime tier certification for either room. Fire protection at both sites is detection rather than gas suppression, which is an ordinary choice at this scale.

Carrier presence at Medford is independently verifiable rather than asserted. PeeringDB lists facility 5084 as Data Center West Medford at 739 Welch Street, Medford, Oregon 97501, with coordinates matching this registry's stored point to within a few metres, and it records four networks present at the site. American Registry for Internet Numbers records identify them as Computer Country, Hunter Communications, LS Networks and Diving Bell Dev LLC, a genuine if modest mix of a Rogue Valley fibre carrier, a Pacific Northwest regional carrier and smaller local providers. The Eugene site is not registered in PeeringDB.

One data quality caveat applies to the rows themselves. Both OpenStreetMap objects carry the name "Date Center West - Eugene", with the typo, yet one sits on Welch Drive in Medford and the other on Willamette Street in Eugene. The Medford row is the company's primary site under a mislabelled Eugene name, not a second Eugene facility. Anyone counting these two rows should read them as two small rooms totalling roughly 2,500 square feet of technical space between them, not as two campuses, and should not infer any megawatt figure from either.
